title: Meta reportedly drops raw AI usage from engineer performance reviews
friendlyTitle: Meta learned that counting AI tokens is a poor way to judge good work
summary: The Decoder, citing an internal memo reported by The Information, says Meta will stop using AI dashboards and token consumption in engineer performance reviews and instead judge the quality, speed and complexity of work. The earlier activity metric reportedly encouraged employees to consume tokens to improve their leaderboard position while internal AI costs rose.
friendlySummary: A report says Meta will no longer rate engineers by how much they use AI. Some workers had used extra tokens to look better on a leaderboard, even when that activity did not prove better results.
whyItMatters: When a company rewards tool use, people optimize the counter rather than the outcome—a familiar management failure with an AI-sized bill. Organizations should measure accepted work, cycle time, defects and total cost, while treating prompts or tokens as diagnostic data rather than employee targets.
friendlyWhyItMatters: People change their behavior to match a target. Measure finished work, quality, mistakes and cost instead of rewarding how often someone uses an AI tool.
